items.title: A representable locally quasi-finite map from an affine formal algebraic space is representable by schemes

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a map of presheaves on the fppf site whose source is an affine formal algebraic space and which is representable by algebraic spaces and locally quasi-finite is representable by schemes (statement lines 2380-2385). The proof tests against a morphism from a scheme: it has to show that the fibre product is a scheme, and it does so on quasi-compact open subspaces. Writing the source as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, the restriction of the projection to such a quasi-compact open subspace factors through one of the stages, and the resulting morphism into a product of that stage with the test scheme is a monomorphism, hence separated, and locally quasi-finite because the given map is; the criterion for a locally quasi-finite separated algebraic space over a scheme then makes each quasi-compact open subspace a scheme, and a criterion for being a scheme in terms of quasi-compact open subspaces finishes the argument (proof lines 2387-2409). The claim is H2: the reduction to quasi-compact open subspaces, the factorisation through a stage, and the two criteria applied at the end are all displayed, and the local quasi-finiteness hypothesis enters exactly once, in the middle step.
